utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Before we start with our proceedings this morning, I just wanted to thank everybody for being here on time and for people on the technical side for the preparing, making this, the arrangements possible for our proceedings this morning. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-66-A, The Prosecutor versus Fatmir Limaj, Haradin Bala, and Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that both counsel for Mr. Limaj and counsel for Mr. Musliu will be with us by teleconference. Because of technological limitations, we can only have one of them with us at a time. Accordingly, for the first few minutes, I wish us to deal exclusively with appeals related to Mr. Bala and to Mr. Musliu. Could I now please have the appearances of the parties in this regard. First the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I'm Shelagh McCall. My co-counsel is Barbara Goy and our case manager is Sebastian Van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. McCall. Counsel for Mr. Bala.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Gregor Guy-Smith appearing on behalf of Mr. Bala with Richard Harvey, my co-counsel, and Bart Willemsen, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. Counsel for Mr. Musliu should also be with us by teleconference. I understand that Mr. Musliu is not currently incarcerated, is not attending the Status Conference. Would his counsel, Mr. Steven Powles, confirm this for the record. Mr. Powles -- thank you, Mr. Powles. Could you please confirm for the record that Mr. Musliu is not attending the Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, that's correct. He has given his consent for the Status Conference to proceed in his absence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Powles, we did indeed receive your filing of yesterday regarding your client's concern that you participate by teleconference. I deem the filing that you provided with the signature on the e-mail to satisfy the requirements under Article 65 bis C for purposes of this particular Status Conference. Now Mr. Bala is present today. I want to make sure that he can follow these proceedings. Mr. Bala, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand? Mr. Bala.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I did not hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I still can't hear anything in English.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Albanian on English channel]

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can interrupt, we're not hearing either...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: What is the problem exactly? Just a second, Mr. Bala. What is happening?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Okay. We'll just wait a moment for the technical problems which have arisen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Could you find out whether we have a good chance of resolving that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: We are okay? Well, we will resume or proceedings then and I will repeat my question to Mr. Bala. I wanted to make sure that you can follow these proceedings, Mr. Bala, and can you hear us and -- in a language that you understand? Mr. Bala.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can he repeat. I did not hear him. Can he come closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Bala, closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can follow. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bala. This is, as you know, is a Status Conference called in accordance with 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. You may sit down, Mr. Bala. You may sit down. This is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis B requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation to and including the mental and physical conditions of that person. The last Status Conference in this case was held on 5 December 2006. As Mr. Bala is currently detained at the UN Detention Centre Unit, Detention Unit, I want to start by asking him whether there are any issues that he would like to raise at this time. Mr. Bala, do you have anything that you wish to say about the conditions of your detention? You did not hear my question?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing to raise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bala. So it is my understanding that you understood my question and that you have no concerns that you would like to raise regarding your mental or physical well-being. If that is correct, you may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT BALA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bala. Now I would like to ask counsel for Mr. Musliu whether there are any issues that Mr. Musliu would like to raise through counsel. So now we are going back to Mr. Powles. Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: No. Thank you very much, Your Honour. Nothing to raise on behalf of Mr. Musliu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Powles. Are you -- also like to let you know that the Appeals Chamber is looking for dates in late May or in June for all our arguments in the appeals. Once we identify more precise dates, we will let the parties know through a scheduling order. Now I would like to check with counsel whether they have any other issues they would like to raise at this time. Counsel, any issues that you would like to raise? I will be to you, Prosecution, in a moment; first the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you asking me, Your Honour, or are you asking Mr. Powles? I just want to make sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, let me start from you, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Surely. Since the Chamber is intending on issuing a scheduling order, I'm wondering whether or not it would be appropriate to request the Chamber, if it seems to be advisable, to issue any questions that might direct the respective parties to focus on those issues that the Chamber might be interested with regard to the appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. This is a practice that we increasingly resort to. And it is likely that we will follow it in this case too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I should mention that I don't take total credit for that. As a matter of fact, it is something that I discussed with the Prosecution prior to today's proceedings beginning and I believe they are of the same mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Guy-Smith and Mr. Powles and then I will go back to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm grateful for the opportunity. Again, nothing to raise on behalf of Mr. Musliu at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So many thanks for your participation, especially at this early hour London time. Before we say good-bye to you, I would ask to you remain by your phone for a few more minutes, first, to hear what the Prosecution would want to say and also, should Mr. Khan with whom we will be speaking with in a moment, raise any issue that would require us to talk to again. So, it's the Prosecution please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's been raised by Mr. Guy-Smith and the Prosecution is of similar mind that it would be very helpful to have questions from the Appeals Chamber. In terms of a time frame for that, Your Honour, the Prosecution would request that, if possible, the Appeals Chamber issue those questions around six weeks in advance of the scheduled hearing date to allow the parties to properly consider the questions and prepare their submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. McCall. As regards the principle of stating the questions in the scheduling order, I think that it is certainly the practice now of the Appeals Chamber and I expect that we will do so again. We will try to issue the scheduling order as early as we can. Whether we can do it a whole six weeks in advance, I cannot promise you, but we will do our best to give you as much advance notice as we can. You have no other questions or points to raise, I would like now -- I will need a short pause for the technical people to establish a connection, a phone connection with Mr. Khan. Mr. Khan, are you with us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Just need ten seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Khan. So you are with us and you can hear me, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Can you please state your appearance for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes. Karim Khan for Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. Before turning to -- I would like simply to inform you, since you have not been listening to our proceedings so far, that both the counsel and the Prosecution have expressed their wish that the scheduling order which we will issue would contain questions to the parties, and the Prosecution has asked for such questions to be stated six weeks in advance. I did indicate to the parties that it is now the practice of the Appeals Chamber to include in scheduling orders questions to the parties, and that we will try to do it as early as possible, but that I cannot promise or commit myself and my colleagues to six weeks' advance notice, but we will do our best to do it early in the day. Now, I note, Mr. Khan, that we have not received any filing from you in relation to Mr. Limaj's written consent for you to participate via teleconference. I understand that you have such a letter, but that it has not yet been filed. I gather that you attempted to file it electronically last night, but I hear that you might not have attached the actual document. If you file the letter within the next two days, I will deem that to be adequate for purposes of Rule 65 bis (C). To recap to you briefly, Mr. Khan, so far in the Status Conference we checked with Mr. Bala as to whether he has any concerns related to his custody and we have asked the other parties to raise any issues in relation to the appeals regarding Mr. Bala and Mr. Musliu. No party has raised any concerns. I've also notified the parties that the Appeals Chamber is looking for dates in late May or in June for the oral arguments in this case and that the Appeals Chamber will issue a scheduling order --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Hello? Yes, I think we got cut off. Hello?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Khan, you're back with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, sir, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I am -- can you tell us at what point we were disconnected? What is the last thing you heard me say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I think Your Honour was saying that you were proposing to issue a scheduling order with a list of questions and then we got disconnected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: You heard what I said about your filing attempts?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Okay. So let me then repeat that for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Khan, I note that we have not received any filing from you in relation to Mr. Limaj's written consent for you to participate via teleconference. I understand that you have such a letter, but it has not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I have indeed and it was -- in addition, it was e-mailed electronically, a filing yesterday, to Jean Galbraith, Martin Petrov, at Court Management Services, and the parties --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes, but the problem is -- but you, perhaps inadvertently, you have not attached the actual document because we have not received with that electronic communication to which you have now referred. So this is what I -- sorry? Here is what I would suggest --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I think if the staff at the Court check, they will have it. There were some problems from Liberia. Also my legal assistant -- I couldn't send any attachments because the signed consent was too large. So my legal assistant here also e-mailed, forwarded my e-mail with the attachment. So I did check yesterday - and I was copied in on it - it was sent to Court Management and the parties as well. So it is -- would be with the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, we will look --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Perhaps after the Status Conference, it will become clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: We will look into that. What I would suggest just in case, you refile the letter within the next two days should we not find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: In which case we would deem that to be adequate filing for the purposes of Rule 65 bis (C).

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So if you could, just in case, do it within the next two days, because I'm not sure that we will so far find it in the ICTY. So far I have not been advised about the arrival of that document. So, please, in conclusion --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: -- you will file the letter within the next two days. Now, Mr. Khan, to recap for you briefly, so far in the Status Conference we checked with Mr. Bala as to whether he has any concerns related to his custody and we have asked the other parties to raise any issues in relation to the appeals regarding Mr. Bala and Mr. Musliu. No party has raised any concerns. I have also notified that the parties that the Appeals Chamber is looking for dates in late May or in June for the oral argument in this case, and that the Appeals Chamber will issue a scheduling order for oral arguments in due course, once we have identified the precise dates, and you did hear the gist of our discussion on questions to the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful. As for Mr. Limaj, there are no questions and no issues, obviously, arising from Mr. Limaj. The only remark I will have about the date for the oral argument in Limaj, of course, is a matter entirely for the Court, is that there is a trial due to start in -- on the 4th of June, the Taylor case I'm involved in, and I don't know if -- how flexible either Court will be to accommodating the court schedule of the other. And perhaps we can wait until there's an order of the Court. But the Taylor case is due to start on the 4th of June, so I hope there won't be a clash.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, I cannot now, as I indicated, give you a precise date and I trust that this matter of coordination, you will be able to resolve it to our mutual satisfaction when the day comes and you know the dates. And maybe the date we will fix will be such as to avoid any conflict, but we will -- we will all try to resolve this matter. But in the event, we except you to find an appropriate solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm most grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I gather, Mr. Khan, therefore, that you have already told us that there are no issues that Mr. Limaj would like to raise from you apart, of course, from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, there are no issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: -- scheduling. Thank you, Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm most grateful. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Now, with regard to Mr. Khan, does the Prosecution wish to add anything? No, the Prosecution does not have any additional issues. Any other issues that the Prosecution would like to raise regarding the appeal of Mr. Limaj, related to Limaj?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Khan, are there any other issues? I take it no?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there's not. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you so very much. I thank the parties for their attendance, especially at this early hour, and I thank the Registry for its work in coordinating this teleconferencing, and I thank the technical people and the interpreters. With that, I call the proceedings to a close. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
